messages:
tom: Noticed 8 duplicate credit memos in NetSuite this morning. Looks tied to Stripe refund webhooks.

liz: Any pattern on invoice ids or timestamps?

tom: All from refunded charge series ch_03X... same customer, sent within a 2s window each.

cole: Stripe should send idempotency via `idempotency_key` or webhook `id` in the header. Are we reading the right field?

tom: Our webhook consumer stores event.id but the retry path in the lambda reprocesses the payload without checking event.id for previous netting. If the lambda retries + the webhook is resent, we create a second refund in NS.

ops-jen: @billing-bot open FIN-4890 and assign to eng (P1) with rollback option.

billing-bot: Created FIN-4890: "Webhook consumer: enforce event.id idempotency + DLQ fix" assigned to @cole, priority P1, link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-4890

cole: Quick mitigation: (1) add a preflight lookup in NetSuite for an existing refund with external_ref=event.id before creating (2) make lambda ack only after write-confirmation, and (3) add short-term dedupe cache (redis) keyed by event.id for 24h.

liz: Approve. Also need a finance-side reconciliation to mark which credit memos to reverse if duplicates already posted. Can you add a CSV export of suspect memos?

cole: Will add `suspect_duplicates_{date}.csv` in s3://redwood-billing/reconciliations/ and attach to FIN-4890. ETA: patch in 3 hrs, deploy in low-traffic window.

tom: Manual fix: I voided 6 of the duplicates in NetSuite; left 2 pending edge-cases where payment refs differed. Adding those to the CSV.

ops-jen: SRE note: retries came from lambda timeout + webhook resend. We should increase visibility on lambda durations to avoid accidental replays.

billing-bot: FIN-4890 updated: comment from @cole with PR link https://git.redwood.ai/billing/commit/ghi789 and reconciliation CSV uploaded.

liz: Thanks. Once deployed, run a backfill to dedupe historical events for the last 48h and cc finance when CSV is ready.

cole: On it. Will run backfill with dry-run first and share logs.
